_standard: Never Silently Cut the Data a Decision Depends On
_what: Sites that bound a value with a bare .slice()/.substring() inside a file that calls a model — either bound to a name and interpolated, or written inline in a multi-line template. Each needs its bound RE-DERIVED against what its consumer accepts, its cut DISCLOSED in-band via src/core/boundedInput.ts, and a judgment on whether the input is load-bearing (in which case the site must REFUSE, not disclose).
_honestScope: This population OVER-INCLUDES on purpose. The detector reads a syntactic shape and cannot tell a prompt from a long error string in the same file, so some entries are out of scope for this article (they bound OUTPUT, which the sibling article governs). Over-inclusion costs a longer review list; under-inclusion costs a missed live bug — and the 2026-08-22 audit proved the under-inclusive version had exactly that. Each entry's classification lives in docs/audits/truncated-judgment-input.md.
_rule: SHRINK-ONLY. Removing an entry is the work — either convert it or mark it exempt with a written reason on the line. Adding one is a regression the lint refuses.
_regenerated: Re-derived 2026-08-22 after the independent review found the inline detector desynchronised by a stray backtick (C4) and the keys unstable under line shifts (C5). The population GREW from 26 to 45 because shape 1 now also sees named-constant bounds, wrapped declarations and substr — the evasions of finding C6, one of which (a named constant) is the style the standard itself prescribes. Four inline entries were removed as parity-bug artifacts, not as fixes.
